answers.core:
This feature should be part of the Godot core rather than an add-on because it relies on engine-level timing APIs (Time.get_ticks_msec() and Time.get_ticks_usec()) for accurate measurement.

A script-based add-on cannot provide the same level of precision reliably across all platforms, especially on mobile and low-end devices where frame rate can vary.

Integrating the HighPrecisionTimer node into the core ensures:

Accurate, frame-independent timing for all projects

Consistency and reliability across devices and platforms

Developers do not have to reimplement the same functionality in scripts

Standardized API for a common need in games (reaction tests, rhythm games, benchmarking, physics, etc.)


Because of these reasons, this feature is best implemented as a core engine node, not as a plugin.
answers.workaround:
It is possible to work around this limitation using a few lines of GDScript, for example:

var start_time := Time.get_ticks_msec()

# later
var elapsed := Time.get_ticks_msec() - start_time
print("Elapsed time: ", elapsed, " ms")

Or using Time.get_ticks_usec() for microsecond precision.

However, this approach has several limitations:

Every developer must reimplement the same logic in their projects

It cannot be easily reused as a node

It does not provide a built-in signal for ticks

Developers may make mistakes or inconsistencies across projects


By providing a dedicated HighPrecisionTimer node, the functionality becomes standardized, reusable, and easy to integrate across all Godot projects. This reduces repetitive scripting and ensures consistency.

title: Add a HighPrecisionTimer node for accurate millisecond/microsecond timing
